reason: In both, the shared receptor internalisation/degradation and LXR-IDOL pathways control LDL-receptor lifetime to limit cholesterol uptake; Y only adds the synthesis side.
Shared SLC anion transporters and their diseases are the core anion/pH-handling and mineralization-failure theme in both; X adds NHE/carbonic anhydrase, Y adds SLC34A2.
Shared glycolysis and creatine/ADP-ATP transport mean ATP generation and buffering in both; X adds lactate/PFK regulation, Y adds oxygen supply.

Target-specific miRNA translational control is the silencing output in both, but miRNA decay/processing regulation is a side 'regulation of regulators' in X and the central control of miRNA abundance in Y.
Shared TRKA-FRS2/ARMS-MAPK-CREB pathways relay NGF signalling to transcription in both stories.
Shared lung branching and epithelial-mesenchymal signalling terms describe the same branched-organ programme in both.
Shared Pol I steps, B-WICH/NoRC and Pol III 5S terms describe rRNA production in both; Y only adds more regulators.
Shared TNFR1-NF-kB, linear ubiquitination and SUMOylation terms form the same NF-kB survival/death switch in both; X adds TLR/IRAK1 input.
Shared PA-DAG-TAG synthesis is the glycerol-phosphate core in both; X adds lysophospholipid recycling, Y adds the phospholipid branch point.
Shared inflammatory cytokine/monocyte activation terms are triggers supporting monocyte recruitment in X but the central myeloid cytokine output with brakes in Y.
Shared di/tricarboxylate transporters move TCA intermediates linked to amino acid nitrogen exchange between compartments in X, but are the core of renal tubular uptake of metabolites in Y.
Shared glucagon-PKA/AMPK-ChREBP/LXR signals switch liver flux between gluconeogenesis and glycolysis in X but coordinate triglyceride storage versus mobilisation in Y.
Shared SLC6A19/SLC6A20/SLC36A2 transport and diseases describe epithelial amino acid reabsorption in both.
Shared cohesin loading and cohesion establishment hold sister chromatids together in both; X adds release, Y adds condensation.
Shared Wnt/Hh lipidation and secretion terms describe lipid modification enabling morphogen release in both, though Y frames it within general palmitoylation.
Shared germline progression and Sertoli barrier terms describe sperm production within the testis niche in both.
Shared tryptophan-kynurenine-NAD and ADP/ATP terms describe making redox and energy cofactors in both.
Shared zinc/copper/manganese transport and toxic-metal detoxification serve essential-metal homeostasis and toxic-metal sequestration in both; Y adds iron.
Shared PAPS/nucleotide-sugar/sulfate supply and hyaluronan turnover provide sulfation and turnover of cartilage glycosaminoglycans in both; Y adds the chain synthesis.
Shared germ cell and ovulation/luteal terms are the core ovarian cycle in X but are the downstream gamete and cyclic outcomes of gonadotropin signalling in Y.
Shared SPM and lipoxin biosynthesis are the resolution mediators in both; X adds catabolism, Y adds hepoxilins/12-LOX products.
Shared P450 and sulfonation terms are the xenobiotic-modification system in both; X adds natural-product substrates, Y adds FMO and acetylation.
Shared oncogenic FLT3-STAT5/CBL signalling is leukaemogenic receptor kinase signalling in both; X adds drug resistance, Y adds PDGFR.
Shared microtubule transport and remodelling terms describe axonal organelle transport protecting motor neurons in both.
Shared NLRP1/NLRP3 inflammasome and IL-1 processing convert danger signals to IL-1 family cytokines in both.
Shared cardiac morphogenesis terms describe building the heart in both stories.
Shared behaviours and amygdala form a broad behavioural-phenotype set (social, reward, motor) in X but are behaviours driven by the stress neuroendocrine system in Y.
Shared replication initiation and E2F/G1-S terms describe S-phase DNA replication in proliferating cells in both.
Shared mitotic and meiotic division machinery describes chromosome segregation in both stories.
Shared adenylate cyclase, PDE1 and CREB terms describe the neuronal cAMP-PKA-CREB pathway in both.
Shared p75NTR and dependence-receptor terms decide neuronal death versus survival in both; Y adds the TRKA arm.
Shared bone/tooth mineralization terms describe hard-tissue mineralization in both; Y adds phosphate endocrine control.
Shared osmosensory responses and renal Na/Cl transport serve cell volume and salt homeostasis in both, though centred on sensing in X and on SLC12 transporters in Y.
Shared GPCR/adenylate cyclase terms regulate insulin and glucagon secretion in both.
Shared TRKA adaptor and MAPK/PI3K/CREB cascades drive neuronal survival and maturation in both.
Shared glutamate reuptake, astrocytic glutamine cycle and vesicular loading describe glutamate recycling at synapses in both.
Shared chondrocyte lineage terms describe cartilage formation from mesenchyme in both.
Shared NOTCH ICD transcription and Notch-HLH terms form the Notch nuclear programme in both.
Shared behaviours and MECP2-GABA are tied to inhibitory signalling and sensorimotor gating in X but are readouts of motor circuits in Y.
Shared toxin uptake and CD163/leishmania terms are scattered pathogen-handling and anti-inflammatory myeloid items in X but toxins are part of the core host-cell entry theme in Y.
Shared PI/PC transfer and PI synthesis describe non-vesicular ER-to-organelle lipid transfer in both.
Shared receptor recycling, endosome and Rab/TBC terms regulate endosome-surface recycling in both, as a branch of Golgi traffic in X and the core in Y.
Shared COPII/COPI terms describe the bidirectional early secretory pathway in both.
Shared TCR-ITK-PKC and thymic differentiation terms describe T cell activation and development in both.
Shared SLC12 cotransport and renal salt transport describe electrolyte reabsorption and cell volume control in both.
Shared IL-12/IFN-gamma/MHC terms describe the Th1 cell-mediated immunity axis in both.
Shared glycosylase recognition, AP-site resolution and NEIL defects describe base excision repair in both.
Shared neural plate patterning terms describe regional division of the embryonic brain in both.
Shared P450/FMO oxidation and conjugation terms describe xenobiotic modification for elimination in both.
Shared 3'-end formation and deadenylation/decay describe making and dismantling mRNA ends to set lifetime in both.
Shared p53 apoptotic gene transcription and regulators are the p53-driven death arm in both; Y adds the arrest arm.
Shared aminoacylation and wobble modifications prepare tRNAs for accurate decoding in both.
Shared IKK/TRAF6/IRAK1 recruitment terms form the receptor hub converging on NF-kB in both.
Shared AMPA/kainate receptors and G-protein modulation describe fast excitatory transmission and its tuning in both.

Shared lipid transfer and lysophospholipid hydrolysis describe moving and turning over membrane lipids in both.

Shared DSB sensing, NHEJ/HR regulation and BRCA defect terms describe double-strand break response and pathway choice in both.
Shared B12 handling and biotin are part of acquiring and activating B-vitamin cofactors in X but are cofactors organised around the propionate pathway and its organic acidaemias in Y.
Shared nucleotide-sugar supply, N/O-glycan and glycosphingolipid synthesis and CDGs describe glycan biosynthesis and its disorders in both.
